answer: Proof-of-Stake acts as a prism through which capital filters influence, forcing agents to lock collateral to participate in consensus. This creates a ridge that an attacker must climb, as the cost of acquiring sufficient tokens to corrupt the network scales linearly with total stake. By weaving a vine of cryptographically signed historical reputation atop this capital lock, the system renders the creation of cheap, ephemeral identities prohibitively expensive, effectively pricing out Sybil adversaries.
